# dsh-freellmapi

**Free-tier multi-provider routing for DeepSeek Harness.**
Eighteen provider entries behind one DSH

provider route — five of them enabled by default, and all five of
those with a free tier — plus a pe

r-request complexity classifier, capability/speed ranking, and automatic
429/5xx failover.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
No external process. No gateway to run. No API key required to get a first answer — the built-in poo

l
contains keyless providers that the maintainer verified with real, credential-free requests.

> ### Unofficial plugin — please read
>
> This is a community project. It is **not** affiliated with

, endorsed by, sponsored by or supported by
> any of the upstream providers it talks to, nor by Deep

Seek. It is not an official DSH plugin.
> Provider names and "DeepSeek Harness" / `@deepseek-ai/*` b

elong to their respective owners.
> Licensed under the MIT License. **You are responsible for comply

ing with each provider's
> terms of service, and for what you send to a free tier that may log and t

provider's
> terms of service, and for what you send to a free tier that may log and train on it.**
## What you get
| **Self-contained routing** | The plugin owns the routing intelligence. `direct` mode (the default)

needs no gateway, no daemon, no Docker — nothing but DSH itself. |
| **A built-in pool of 17 provid
ers / 46 models** | Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter, Mistral, Z.ai (Zhipu), Volcengine Ark, LongCat, LLM7
, Kilo, NVIDIA NIM and OVH AI Endpoints, plus the six 0.7.0 additions — ModelScope (魔搭), iFlytek Spa
rk (讯飞星火), SiliconFlow (硅基流动), SambaNova, HuggingFace Router and Routeway — with per-model capabilit
y, speed, context window, vision and tool-calling facts. **Only five of the seventeen are enabled ou

t of the box.** |
| **Per-request complexity routing** | Every request is scored and classified `sim
ple` / `medium` / `complex`; the tier decides whether capability or speed dominates the ranking. A o

ne-line "list the files here" and a 12-tool refactoring task do not go to the same model. |
| **Auto
matic failover** | A rate-limited (429), broken (5xx), timed-out or `model_unavailable` candidate is
parked and the next-ranked one is tried — **only before the first chunk has been sent**, so a singl

e answer is never spliced from two models. |
| **Health tracking and cooldowns** | The **first retry
able failure already parks** the candidate (2 minutes), and each further consecutive failure escalat
es one step: 2 m → 10 m → 1 h → 24 h. `Retry-After` from the provider always wins; a rejected creden
tial (401/403) parks that provider for 24 h. The scoring penalty decays with a 60-second half-life,

so a single 429 is never a life sentence. |
| **Zero-config start** | Kilo and LLM7 answer without a

ny credential; a fresh install has a non-empty candidate pool before you configure anything. |
| **H
onest diagnostics** | One log line per request names the tier, the winner and how many candidates we

re tried; every failure is an in-band `finish` chunk with a stable code, never an exception. |

## Limitations and unverified claims
Stated plainly, so you know what you are relying on:
1. **The complexity classifier is a heuristic, not understanding.** It counts tokens, fenced code, t

ool
schemas and vocabulary. When it gets it wrong shows
three real misjudgements from this implement

ation. When you know better, pin `auto:simple` /
`auto:medium` / `auto:complex`, or pin one `provide

r/model`.
2. **No end-to-end run against real providers.** Every test in this repository runs agains

t in-process
mock providers, deliberately, so CI stays offline. The only *real* external calls ever

made were the
maintainer's keyless probe (five requests, four 200s and one 404 documented in
`_lead/

live-probe-2026-10-13.md`) plus the credential-free reachability and catalog probes behind the
reach
ability section above (`_lead/research/reachability-v0.7.md`, 2026-10-15). **No completion has ever
been requested with a real key**, so everything else — every keyed provider, every quota number, eve

ry
model id except the ones a public catalog publishes — is **documentation-level evidence**, not
me

asurement.
3. **Only credential-free requests were ever made.** `groq`, `cerebras`, `openrouter`, `m

istral`,
`nvidia` and the rest were contacted without credentials (status codes and public catalogs

only, never a
completion), so their `baseURL`s and model ids come from upstream's registry and migra

tions. Rate-limit
numbers are the 2026-04 baseline and will drift.
4. **`zhipu` is the riskiest entr

y in the pool**, and `volcengine` / `longcat` model ids are inferred —
all three ship **disabled** w

ith `confidence: 'speculative'`. Enabling them is you accepting that risk.
The `zhipu` hostname in p

articular differs between the mainland and overseas sites and the keys do not
interchange: a wrong h

ostname is a guaranteed 401.
5. **Free catalogs drift.** The same model id can answer 200 today and

`400 model_unavailable` tomorrow.
The router treats that as a per-model condition (park + next candi

date), so it degrades instead of
failing — but it is normal operation, not a bug.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
| Component | Supported | Notes |
| DeepSeek Harness runtime | `0.2.0-rc.2` (written and verified against it) | Other `0.2.0-rc.x` bui

lds are likely fine; only stable LLM seam APIs are used |
| Node.js | `>= 22` | Matches the referenc

e DSH plugins |
| Provider APIs | OpenAI-compatible `POST {baseURL}/chat/completions` with SSE | Eve

rything in the pool speaks the same wire |
| `dsh-freellmapi` | `0.7.18` | Zero runtime dependencies
; the DSH LLM runtime is resolved at load time; peers are `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (the config sch

ema) and the optional `@deepseek-ai/cordis` |
| freellmapi gateway | `v0.13.x` protocol surface | On
ly relevant in `gateway` mode |

> Version-numbering note: the upstream gateway's releases are `v0.13.x`, while the npm CLI package
>
`freellmapi` (which provides `setup-dsh`) is versioned independently (e.g. `0.8.1`). Do not treat t

he two
> numbers as the same series.
